title: Charity from the right hand
hookLine: give so the left hand doesn't know what the right gave (Bukhari)

lines: NAMES ON A SCREEN, BIGGEST FIRST.
A LEFT HAND THAT DOESN'T KNOW.
cards: You've seen the photo. Someone hands a sandwich to a man sleeping on the street, and a friend films it from just the right angle. Or the charity gala where the donors' names go up on a screen, biggest first.
Giving has a way of turning into a performance. One hadith goes right at the wish to be seen, with a picture so odd it's hard to forget: a left hand that has no idea what the right hand just did.

teach.b: It's in Bukhari and Muslim: seven people whom Allah will shade on a day when there's no shade but His. A just ruler. A young person who grew up in worship.
Someone whose heart is attached to the mosque. Two people who love each other for Allah's sake. A man called to sin by a woman of rank and beauty, who says, I fear Allah.
Someone who remembered Allah alone, and whose eyes filled with tears.
And the one for today: a person who gave charity and hid it, so that the left hand didn't know what the right hand gave. Your own hand, inches away, never finds out.
That's how quiet it's meant to be: no photo, no mention at dinner, not even a proud glance at yourself. The Qur'an is gentle about it, not absolute.

teach.h: OPENLY IS WELL; HIDDEN IS BETTER.
teach.b: Surah al-Baqarah says that if you give openly, that is well, but if you hide it and give it to the poor, it is better for you.
Open giving can encourage others, and some scholars say the yearly zakat may be given openly for that reason.
But the commentators say the hidden gift protects two people: the one who receives, who keeps their dignity, and the one who gives, whose heart stays clean of showing off.
The same surah warns against cancelling your charity with reminders and hurt. People tell a story, found in later collections, about Ali Zayn al-Abidin, a great-grandson of the Prophet ﷺ.

teach.h: SACKS AT THE DOOR IN THE NIGHT.
teach.b: For years, poor families in Medina found sacks of food at their doors at night, and never knew who brought them.
When he died, they say, the deliveries stopped, and marks were found on his back from carrying them.

how: Muslims are encouraged to give voluntary charity quietly, without mention, following the hadith of the seven shaded and 2:271, while some scholars allow zakat to be given openly to encourage others.

o: money given to the poor on a holy night
a gift given so quietly no one knows who gave it
charity given only to people you know well

games.q: what's inside charity from the right hand — tap the pairs.
p: doesn't know what the right gave
openly is well, hidden is better

s: the Qur'an forbids giving charity openly
2:271 says giving openly is well; hiding it is better for you.
one of the seven shaded hid his charity from his own left hand
so the left hand didn't know what the right gave (Bukhari, Muslim).
the story of Zayn al-Abidin's night sacks is in Sahih al-Bukhari
it's a story people tell, found in later collections.

games.q: you've just paid a stranger's bill at the pharmacy. a friend saw, and asks if they can post about it. what does the hadith point to?
o: keep it hidden, so the left hand doesn't know
post it, but without your name
games.why: the one shaded gave so quietly the left hand didn't know. the Qur'an allows open giving, but calls hidden giving better.

practice: Think of someone who could use something, a coffee, a bag of groceries, a donation made in no one's name, and plan it so no one finds out: not them, not your friends, not your feed.
Notice the little voice that wants someone to know; don't fight it or obey it; just let it be there. If you pray, you can intend it for Allah alone.

wordCard.voice: Secret charity, giving so quietly that your left hand doesn't know, one of the seven shaded on the last day.

orig.note: Arabic: secret charity, the hidden gift.

carryVoice: Your line: hidden is best. Not even your left hand needs to know. One hundred fifty days now.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1423; Sahih Muslim 1031 (the seven shaded)
Qur'an 2:271 (openly is well; hidden is better)
Qur'an 2:264 (do not cancel charity with reminders and hurt)
Abu Nu'aym, Hilyat al-Awliya' (Zayn al-Abidin's night deliveries)
